sections.title: Name and recognition
sections.text: Psilocybe silvatica (Peck) Singer & A.H. Sm. is the currently accepted name for this very small brown agaric; its basionym is Psathyra silvatica Peck. In the protologue, Peck describes a bell-shaped cap 8–10 mm across, dark brown and striate when wet, becoming grey-brown as it dries; the gills are ascending, distant, ferruginous brown with a white edge, and the stem is slender, hollow and slightly flexuous. Later descriptions add a viscid, hygrophanous surface and gills that darken toward purplish-brown. A slight bluish tint has been mentioned in some accounts, but several North American descriptions do not report it; it is not a dependable identification character. This American species is morphologically similar to P. medullosa, a distinct European species in the 2015 phylogenetic study.

sections.title: Habitat
sections.text: Typical records place it in woodland, on mossy ground and plant debris; the epitype published in 2015 was collected in a group on fir debris in Newfoundland. These records support a saprotrophic ecology but do not establish an exclusive host tree or habitat. Collections are rare, and older identifications may be uncertain.

sections.title: Chemical evidence and caution
sections.text: Some books have called it psychoactive by analogy, but Borovička et al. (2015) report that no chemical analysis of P. silvatica had been published at that time. The sources consulted therefore do not confirm its chemistry or any psychoactive effect. Edibility is not established: do not consume it or use this entry to identify a wild collection. Small brown agarics are difficult to distinguish, and a photograph cannot confirm a species.

traits: Very small bell-shaped, hygrophanous cap, dark brown when wet and paler as it dries
Attached gills, grey-brown at first then dark purplish-brown at maturity
Slender, often flexuous, hollow stem; bluing is inconsistent and not diagnostic
Mossy woodland ground and plant debris; the Newfoundland epitype was on fir debris
Rare North American species, distinct from the European Psilocybe medullosa
safetyNote: Chemical composition and edibility are not established in the sources consulted. Do not consume it or infer psychoactive effects or identity from this entry or its image. If accidental ingestion is followed by symptoms, promptly contact a poison centre or medical service.
